original_question: Let Φ = {Φ0 , Φ1 , Φ2 , Φ3 } be a subset of the body (= skew − f ield) H of the real quaternions with the conditions Φp Φ̄q + Φq Φ̄p = 2δp,q , Omega is a domain in R4 = C^2 . On the H-bimodule C 1 (Omega; H) the operator DΦ = P3 k ∂ k=0 Φ ∂xk defines the set of the (lef t − Φ)-hyper-holomorphic functions MΦ (Omega; H) = KerDΦ . Let Φ̂ = {1, i, j, −k} with i, j, k being the ordinary imaginary units in H. It is known that Hol(Omega; C^2 ) ⊂ MΦ̂ (Omega; H), where Hol(Omega; C^2 ) is the subset of all holomorphic (in the usual sense) mappings. 1) Describe the set of all hyper-holomorphic but non-holomorphic functions in Omega (it is not empty). 2) Describe ”locations” of the sets Hol and MΦ Hol inside MΦ . 3) How do they depend on Omega?
target_in_paper: The quaternionic-analysis open problem in The Several Complex Variables Problem List asking for a description of (left-Φ)-hyper-holomorphic quaternion-valued functions on Ω ⊂ C^2 ≅ R^4 that are not ordinary holomorphic, and for the precise relation between the holomorphic class and the full hyper-holomorphic class for the standard structural set Φ̂ = {1, i, j, -k}.
correct_elements: Your draft already captures almost all of the mathematical substance of the problem-list item: the ambient skew field H of real quaternions, the structural-set condition Φp Φ̄q + Φq Φ̄p = 2δp,q, the domain Ω ⊂ R^4 = C^2, the left Cauchy-Riemann-Fueter-type operator DΦ on C^1(Ω; H), the kernel MΦ(Ω; H) of left-Φ-hyper-holomorphic functions, the special structural set Φ̂ = {1, i, j, -k}, the inclusion Hol(Ω; C^2) ⊂ MΦ̂(Ω; H), and the three intended tasks: identify hyper-holomorphic but non-holomorphic functions, locate the holomorphic class inside the hyper-holomorphic class, and understand the dependence on Ω.
missing_details: The comparison with ordinary holomorphy requires the standard identification H ≅ C^2, typically q = z1 + z2 j; this should be stated explicitly.
The bar in Φ̄q should be identified as quaternionic conjugation.
The operator DΦ should be stated explicitly as left multiplication: DΦ = Σ_{k=0}^3 Φk ∂/∂xk acting on C^1(Ω; H).
The problem really specializes to the standard structural set Φ̂ when comparing with ordinary holomorphic maps; the general Φ only sets up the framework.
The phrase "MΦ Hol" is incomplete/garbled; the intended set is almost certainly the set difference MΦ̂(Ω; H) \ Hol(Ω; C^2), or equivalently the hyper-holomorphic but non-holomorphic part.

The word "locations" is too vague for a stand-alone research question; it should be replaced by a request to describe the relative position, decomposition, or inclusion structure of the relevant subclasses inside MΦ̂(Ω; H).
It should be made explicit that Hol(Ω; C^2) means ordinary complex-holomorphic maps on the domain Ω ⊂ C^2.
The statement should clarify that the dependence question ranges over domains Ω ⊂ C^2, with no boundedness or topological restriction stated in the draft.

The parenthetical remark that the set of hyper-holomorphic but non-holomorphic functions is nonempty is contextual information, not part of the main question, and should be separated from the problem statement.
refined_question: Let H be the skew field of real quaternions, let Ω ⊂ C^2 ≅ R^4 be a domain, and let Φ = {Φ0, Φ1, Φ2, Φ3} ⊂ H be a structural set satisfying Φp Φ̄q + Φq Φ̄p = 2δp,q. On C^1(Ω; H) define DΦ = Σ_{k=0}^3 Φk ∂/∂xk and MΦ(Ω; H) = ker DΦ. For the standard structural set Φ̂ = {1, i, j, -k}, identify H with C^2 by q = z1 + z2 j, so that the ordinary holomorphic maps Hol(Ω; C^2) are viewed as a subclass of MΦ̂(Ω; H). Describe the genuinely quaternionic part MΦ̂(Ω; H) \ Hol(Ω; C^2), and determine precisely how the holomorphic class Hol(Ω; C^2) and its non-holomorphic complement sit inside MΦ̂(Ω; H), including how this picture depends on the choice of the domain Ω.
justification: arXiv:math/9509202 is itself a problem list rather than a theorem/conjecture paper, so the target here is a standalone open-problem entry, not something labeled Conjecture 1.1 or Theorem 1.3. The draft is already very close to a direct transcription of that item. The main refinements needed to make it fully stand-alone and paper-faithful are: (i) make the H ≅ C^2 identification explicit, because ordinary holomorphy is otherwise undefined in this context; (ii) repair the garbled expression "MΦ Hol" to the intended hyper-holomorphic-but-non-holomorphic class; and (iii) replace the informal word "locations" by a precise request about the relative position of subclasses inside MΦ̂(Ω; H). Because the arXiv HTML for math/9509202 exposes only metadata/abstract and not the internal problem-list item text, the exact item number and printed page of this quaternionic entry could not be recovered from the source via the available interface; the formulation above therefore keeps as close as possible to your draft while normalizing the notation and scope against later primary-source context on the same holomorphic-versus-regular quaternionic question.
